There are some old, crusty veterans who think that any forward progress (wheels, v-hull, improved ballistic/IED protection) is sacrilege no matter what, because the tracks and inboard thrusters are being removed.   The new versions will be much faster on land, and the same speed in the water.  I can't tell you how many times I fucking hated the 40-50 yr-old design of those things.  While the guns were adequate for the vehicle's intended purpose, the turret itself was ancient, too small, optics were shit, nightvision was from the stone-age (if it worked at all) and everything was already broken from the previous operators.  The transmissions were weak, which required that the engines (the one shining star on the vehicle) needed to be detuned so the torque didn't shred gearbox internals.   Comms were fucking old radios.  Four of them.  That's four radios, which on their own were old as fuck, but still reliable, yet were at the mercy of the shoddy electrical system in the vehicle.  Even following correct vehicle startup/shutdown procedures resulted in far too many dumped fills and lost crypto.   SOP was basically this: Ignore any ballistic protection that the turret/vehicle might provide and stick your head out of the turret/driver's hatch so you can see where you're going during the day, and especially at night. At night there are no functioning night-vision systems built into the vehicle that work for shit....    DVE?  Yeah, you're fucking high.  That shit is a 2D thermal scope that will still let you crash into something at more than 3mph.  At least you can use it to see the fish under water.... if it worked at all.  Crew chief?  Yeah I'm up there with NVGs trying to see where I'm going, and relay to my driver who's 8ft. away, can't hear me because any number of Comm. issues has decided to pop up right as we're stepping off.   There were some pros to the vehicle designed by a tuna boat builder.  You can hide limitless amounts of contraband in them.  They are so old, there are about 17 moving parts, total.   Also make a great camping vehicle.

Ever been to the beach?   The sand there is pretty compact.  I actually drive my car on the beaches where I live all the time.  Also, the new vehicles are 8x8, or all-wheel drive, or whatever you want to call it.  They aren't getting stuck on a beach.

Ease maintenance.  If you lose a tire/wheel then the vehicle can still push forward through whatever.   The current vehicle has two tracks, and if you throw track then you're screwed.  So very, very, screwed.   Also, the final drives on the vehicle are weak. Six or seven feel of concertina wire will kill them if it gets wrapped up in there.  The tracks are expensive,  and the individual trackpads don't last for a long time, which means that you have to break track, unroll the fucker, and then remove/replace the individual trackpads.  This can be a huge pain in the ass, because the bolts that secure the trackpad to the track itself are usually rusted solid, and need to be cut out with a torch because your two breaker bars are missing/broken, and no one in the unit has ever had the forethought to buy impact guns.   Of course, there's only like two people in the unit that are authorized to use a cutting torch, and they're usually both on leave, or FAP'd out to the range or something.
-Chesty Puller, USMC
